title: Where do your PDFs actually go? A plain-English guide to PDF privacy
excerpt: Understand local PDF processing, ordinary website requests and practical checks before working with a sensitive document.
author: The MY PDF FIX Team
body:
## Local processing is about document contents

When you choose a file in a browser, the page can read it after your selection. A server-based converter sends document data to another system for processing. A local converter reads and transforms it on your device. Neither label alone describes every connection made by the website.

PDF Fix Hub's 25 tools process selected documents in your browser. [Merge PDF](/merge-pdf), [Split PDF](/split-pdf) and the other tools do not upload document contents for conversion. The site still needs network requests to load its pages, scripts and processing modules. Some content pages also load Google's AdSense ownership-verification script, with advertising requests initially paused. Optional analytics and advertising follow your privacy choices; see the [Cookie Policy](/cookie-policy).

This means “document contents are not uploaded,” rather than “the browser makes no connections.” It is also not a guarantee against a compromised device, a malicious extension or someone who can access your downloads.

## A harmless file is the best first check

Use a made-up document before selecting personal records. For example, create a PDF containing only “Privacy practice document,” then try [PDF to Text](/pdf-to-text). The output should contain text that was already embedded in that sample. Scanned pages need OCR, which that tool does not provide.

If you are comfortable with browser developer tools, open the Network panel before selecting the sample. Clear the log, run the operation and look for requests carrying document data. Normal requests for JavaScript or fonts are different from an uploaded file. This check can help you understand behavior, but an unfamiliar request or a quiet network log is not a complete security audit.

Trying a task offline can provide another clue only after all required code has loaded. A tool may need a module the first time you use it, so an offline failure does not prove that your document is being uploaded. PDF Fix Hub does not promise a fully installed offline application.

## Choose the right output for sensitive information

Local processing does not make every editing method suitable for confidentiality. [Edit PDF](/edit-pdf) adds overlays. A whiteout rectangle can cover a name visually while leaving the underlying text recoverable. [Crop PDF](/crop-pdf) changes the visible page boundary; it is not secure redaction either.

[Edit Metadata](/edit-pdf-metadata) clears selected document properties, not every hidden object. Creation dates, embedded metadata, comments or attachments can remain. Use a dedicated redaction or sanitization workflow when actual removal is required, then independently inspect the result.

## Handle originals and downloads deliberately

Keep an original in a location you control. Check your browser's download folder, shared-device access and any automatic cloud backup before processing confidential material. Do not send private PDFs or passwords in a support email. If a task fails, report the tool name, browser and error text using a harmless reproduction instead.

The [Privacy Policy](/privacy) explains the site's data practices. For workplace documents, follow your organization's rules even when the conversion itself happens locally.
